To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the reliability of an N-version software system is a function of the software fault detection capability, the coverage of the error detection and recovery mechanisms, the failure rates of the hardware components and the number of versions of the software.

(1) the probability of a software error in the NVP application is approximately 0.1% per year, (2) the probability of an undetected hardware error in the N-version application is approximately 1% per year.

(a) software faults are the primary cause of failures in an NVP system and (b) hardware faults are also an important factor in the reliability of the overall system, especially when the coverage is low.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reliability analysis of NVP systems and the development of a methodology for analyzing systems designed to tolerate both software faults and transient and permanent hardware faults.
the development of a quantitative model for the reliability evaluation of an N-version program system.
the development and analysis of a model for a system designed to achieve fault tolerance in the face of both software and hardware faults.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the system is reliable.
the reliability of an N-version program is a function of many variables.
the NVP system is reliable and that its reliability increases with time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current NVP paradigm can provide high system reliability, but the reliability estimates are highly dependent on the coverage of hardware faults and the software fault model.
the current design paradigm for NVP is effective in achieving fault tolerance in the presence of independent faults.

a quantitative reliability analysis is a necessary step in the design of fault-tolerant systems, since the reliability estimates provide a basis for comparing the cost-effectiveness of various design alternatives.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a reliability analysis is an important part of any design process for an NVP system.
it is important for system designers to consider both hardware faults and software faults in their system analysis.
a quantitative reliability analysis is necessary for the design of a reliable NVP system, and that such an analysis should consider both the hardware and the software aspects of the design.
